findings.evidence: The request's constraints note that the current proposal uses one shared password for all workers.
findings.rationale: A single shared password for all workers removes individual accountability and defeats central identity verification for a system holding SSNs and medical data.

findings.evidence: The request's constraints note that the current proposal stores attachments in a publicly readable folder.
findings.rationale: Placing medical attachments and identity records in a location readable by the public exposes restricted data without any confidentiality control.
Without knowing the hosting environment, reviewers cannot confirm the required network, identity, and logging controls are in place before production launch.
findings.missingInformation: The request does not state whether the application will run inside an approved state cloud boundary with the required security controls.

findings.rationale: Collecting name, address, and SSN triggers a mandatory privacy review that has not been documented as complete.
findings.missingInformation: There is no confirmation that an approved privacy threshold assessment covering lawful basis, retention, and downstream recipients exists before collecting applicant name, address, and SSN.

findings.rationale: Medical attachments and eligibility decisions are restricted data requiring a signed data sharing agreement and role-based access, neither of which is confirmed.
findings.missingInformation: It is not stated whether a signed data sharing agreement with the originating program limits access to the medical and eligibility data to named staff by role.

findings.rationale: Selecting appropriate production security controls depends on a formal classification of the identity, SSN, and medical data categories, which the request marks as unresolved.
findings.missingInformation: The accountable program owner has not classified the data categories (identity, address, SSN, medical attachments) this application will store or process.

findings.rationale: No organization has been identified to accept operational responsibility for this service before it can move toward production.
findings.missingInformation: The request does not name an owning organization responsible for service health, incident response, support, and end-of-life decisions.

findings.rationale: Recording an application decision without defined retention and audit requirements risks losing the evidence and accountability needed for later review.
findings.missingInformation: Retention requirements for the application decision, its supporting evidence, and the deciding staff member's identity are not established.

findings.evidence: The request specifies that translations must be reviewed by a qualified translator and both notices need plain-language editing before a named approver signs off.
findings.rationale: The request already commits to translator review and plain-language editing, which aligns with the language access requirement, but the described process should be documented as the qualifying human approval before release.
The acceptance criteria only mention a screen-reader check, leaving unclear whether the PDFs will also receive the reading-order, alt-text, and title remediation the standard requires.
findings.missingInformation: Whether the accessible PDF production process will verify logical reading order, alternative text for any images, and a document title in addition to the screen-reader pass.

findings.rationale: If a machine translation tool drafts the initial English or Spanish text, a named human reviewer's approval or disagreement should be recorded before the notice is finalized.
findings.missingInformation: Whether the translations will be drafted with a machine translation or generative tool, and if so, who is the named staff reviewer recording approval of that output.
